html:
The Ute are a Native American people of the Great Basin and the Rocky Mountains, in what is now Colorado and Utah. The state of Utah is named after them.

They speak a Numic language of the Uto-Aztecan family, close to that of the Southern Paiute and the Shoshone. They lived in bands that moved between mountain valleys and plains, hunting deer, elk and bison and gathering seeds and roots.

The Ute were among the first peoples north of Spanish New Mexico to gain horses, in the 1600s. They traded hides and captives at New Mexico fairs and alternately raided and allied with the Spanish, the Navajo and the Jicarilla. For a time they rode with the Comanche, then fought them.

After a clash at the White River Agency in 1879, the US forced most Ute out of Colorado. Today there are three Ute tribes: the Ute Mountain Ute, the Southern Ute and the Northern Ute of the Uintah and Ouray Reservation in Utah.
